key_insight: Large-scale noisy quantum hardware can accurately simulate dissipative spin-1/2 Heisenberg chains and map their nonequilibrium steady-state phase diagram.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that superconducting processors can tackle open quantum many-body problems at sizes and depths beyond classical reach, making them a practical platform for scientific simulation of dissipative quantum systems.
method: Simulated Lindblad dynamics on IBM superconducting hardware using Stinespring dilation.
Ran chains up to 50 sites with up to 100 simultaneously active qubits and entangling-gate depths up to 1700.
Measured static structure factors to identify steady-state magnetic phases across the Jx–Jy plane.
evidence_signal: The authors report 117 hardware data points and phase identification of ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, spin-density-wave, and paramagnetic steady states.
watch_item: Because the dissipation is implemented through Trotterization and hardware noise acts as an additional weak dissipator, the observed phases may include Trotter-induced or device-dependent effects.
paper_title: Large-scale quantum simulations of dissipative spin-1/2 Heisenberg chains
